sources.title: California Department of Public Health, All Facilities Letter AFL 25-17, SNF Discharge Notice Requirements
sources.notes: The 2026-08-30 standing packet recorded cdph.ca.gov as returning an incomplete certificate chain to curl and to python/certifi, and captured this source through the session's HTTP fetch tool. Retested 2026-09-04: plain curl with a browser user-agent now returns 200 with the full page, including the eight-item notice-contents list, the four 30-day exceptions and the 'basis under Title 42 CFR section 483.15(c)(1)(i)(A)-(F)' phrase the standing page quotes verbatim. Whatever blocked it on 2026-08-30 no longer does, consistent with the transient-failure pattern CLAUDE.md records for Arkansas's codeofarrules.arkansas.gov. #DeltaPlaceHolderMain is this SharePoint template's own content well, narrower than body (which also carries the site's mega-menu) and wider than any single paragraph; it includes the page's own masthead furniture ('KAREN L. SMITH, MD, MPH' over a governor line reading 'EDMUND G. BROWN JR.' above a May 28, 2025 letter) exactly as the 2026-08-30 packet recorded a similar mismatched-masthead artifact — reproduced as published, not corrected. strip-zero-width removes the SharePoint editor's own U+200B runs between paragraphs (visible as nothing to a reader); it does not touch the curly apostrophes and quotation marks the letter itself prints, which are left exactly as the publisher set them.

sources.title: California Department of Health Care Services, Office of Administrative Hearings and Appeals — Transfer Discharge and Refusal to Readmit Unit
sources.notes: The 2026-08-30 standing packet recorded dhcs.ca.gov as returning a 212-byte script shell to curl and captured this source through the session's HTTP fetch tool. sources.notes: The 2026-08-30 standing packet was captured the same way (curl, browser user-agent) and recorded its own method as a tag strip over the <main> element; this template in fact carries no <main> tag, and '#main-content' omits the site's own top navigation ('About Us', 'Providers & Partners', ...) that the standing packet's body plainly carries ('Skip Navigation Links', 'About Us', 'Careers with CDA', ...). sources.title: 22 CCR 72527, Patients' Rights
sources.source_date: last substantively amended 6-23-2011 (Register 2011, No. 25); database current through 8/28/26, Register 2026, No. 35 (both per the document's own Currentness/history text)
sources.notes: The 2026-08-30 standing packet recorded govt.westlaw.com/calregs as serving rule bodies only to a scripted client, returning a 4.8 KB shell with no rule text to direct capture, and left 72527 capture-pending. That test used the GUID printed on DHCS's own page (I71F6A1A0A39811E08822C131FF5E2170), which returns 'Document not found' from a real browser as well as from curl -- the GUID itself is stale, not the transport. Found again 2026-09-04 by browsing govt.westlaw.com/calregs from its own home page (Title 22 > Division 5 > Chapter 3 > Article 5, no search box or session token involved) to the section's current address, IBAE556025B6111EC9451000D3A7C4BC3, which a plain curl with a browser user-agent resolves directly with no session cookie. This is a stale-link problem, not a scripted-client-over-an-API problem, so it is captured as an ordinary curl source rather than under the agency-API rule. #co_document is the platform's own per-section container: it holds the breadcrumb, the section heading, currentness marker, full text, Credits/NOTE, HISTORY and the 'This database is current through' line, and excludes the page's site chrome and the 'Documents In Sequence' footer navigation.

sources.title: 22 CCR 72519, Patient Transfer
sources.source_date: no HISTORY entries printed in the document's own text (Credits/NOTE only); database current through 8/28/26, Register 2026, No. 35
sources.notes: Same host, method and scope as Sources 5 and 6, found the same way while reading Article 5's section list (this rule immediately precedes 72520 there). Not linked by either AFL 25-17 or the DHCS OAHA page; captured because its own text cross-references 'Section 72527(a)(5)', which after 72527's 2011 renumbering names a different right (informed consent) than the transfer/discharge right at 72527(a)(6) -- a discrepancy inside the state's own current regulations, recorded as a finding rather than corrected.

sources.title: 22 CCR 51535.1, Bed Hold for Acute Hospitalization
sources.source_date: last operative amendment 12-24-2013, Certificate of Compliance filed 5-22-2014 (Register 2014, No. 21); database current through 8/28/26, Register 2026, No. 35
sources.notes: Found 2026-09-04 by following 72520(a)(2)'s own cross-reference ('Except as provided in Section 51535.1') and browsing to it (Title 22 > Division 3 > Subdivision 1 > Chapter 3 > Article 7's own section list, no search box). Same host, method and #co_document scope as Sources 5-7. This is the Medi-Cal reimbursement counterpart to 72520's licensing bed-hold rule: it states the same seven-day cap for payment purposes and adds the procedural detail (physician notice, day-of-departure/day-of-return counting, termination on death) that 72520 does not. Its own printed payment-rate table runs only through fiscal year 2006-07 despite the section's 'Currentness' marker and a 2013-2014 amendment to the same subsection; both facts are quoted rather than reconciled.

sources.title: Welfare and Institutions Code section 14126.029 (facility compliance with an OAHA hearing decision)
sources.source_date: added by Stats. 2021, Ch. 143, Sec. 384, effective July 27, 2021; conditionally operative per section 14126.035(a) and inoperative after December 31, 2027 per section 14126.036, both per the document's own closing credit line
sources.notes: Same host, method and scope as Source 4. Found 2026-09-04 searching for any California statement of what happens once an OAHA hearing is decided, beyond HSC 1599.1(h)'s Medi-Cal-eligible refusal-to-readmit case; it states a facility must comply within three calendar days of service of an OAHA decision finding an improper transfer, discharge, or refusal to readmit, on pain of a per-day penalty, and applies to TDA and RTR decisions alike rather than only the RTR/Medi-Cal case. It is a post-decision compliance deadline, not a pendency statement (it does not say whether a resident stays in place while the hearing is pending), and its own closing credit line states it is conditionally operative on a skilled-nursing quality-assurance fee remaining approved by CMS and is 'Inoperative after December 31, 2027' -- both quoted rather than assessed, because whether the operative condition is currently met is not a fact this capture can verify.
